tagline: Mountain curves and fifteen overlooks, built after a campaign by covered wagon.
intro: The Cherohala Skyway curves through the Cherokee and Nantahala national forests on two lanes with wide shoulders. There are 15 scenic overlooks, and grades reach 9%. Allow two hours for the drive, the archived America’s Byways page advises. The national byway program presented this National Scenic Byway as a journey through Appalachian forests, highlighting mile-high views, fall foliage and the cultural heritage of the Cherokee tribe and early settlers.

The campaign for the Cherohala Skyway traveled by covered wagon. At the Tellico Plains Kiwanis Club, Sam Williams proposed a wagon train to publicize the need for a road between Tennessee and North Carolina. On July 4, 1958, 67 wagons and 325 horseback riders made the trip to Murphy, North Carolina. By 1962, Charles Hall and fellow advocates were asking Congress for money; the first federal appropriation followed that year. Construction was underway by 1967. Hall described a delay of about 13 years while the road’s backers worked with 21 environmental groups. The road cost more than $100 million and reached dedication on October 12, 1996.

From Tellico Plains and the Tellico River, the drive gains more than 4,000 feet to Haw Knob’s slopes near the state line. Unicoi Crest overlooks the Tellico River valley; farther east, Big Junction Overlook faces south between Haw Knob and Big Junction. Beyond Hooper Bald, continue to Santeetlah Gap, where Kilmer Road branches toward Joyce Kilmer Memorial Forest, then follow NC 143 toward Robbinsville.
notice: At Unicoi Crest on the state line, the overlook faces the Tellico River valley.

moments.title: Haw Knob
moments.text: Haw Knob puts one summit in two states and two national forests. At 5,472 feet, it straddles Monroe County, Tennessee, and Graham County, North Carolina. Cherokee lies on the Tennessee side, Nantahala on the North Carolina side: the same pair that gave Cherohala its name. The skyway reaches its own high point on these slopes, just over 5,400 feet after gaining more than 4,000 feet from Tellico Plains. The road carries you along the mountain; the Benton MacKaye Trail reaches the summit and crosses several Unicoi peaks on its course through the Southern Appalachian Mountains.
moments.notice: At Big Junction Overlook, the view faces south from the gap between Haw Knob and Big Junction.

moments.title: Hooper Bald
moments.text: Around 1911, Whiting Manufacturing Company official George Gordon Moore tried to establish a boar hunting preserve atop Hooper Bald. He stocked a 500-acre enclosure with Russian blue boars imported from Europe. The enclosure did not keep most of them in: they escaped to remote slopes and stream bottoms. The introduced boars thrive here, and forest officials consider them a nuisance because they cause erosion in local watersheds. The bald itself is a grassy summit in Nantahala National Forest, rising to 5,429 feet. The half-mile Hooper Bald Trail leads to the top.
moments.notice: The half-mile Hooper Bald Trail reaches a grassy summit.

moments.title: Joyce Kilmer Memorial Forest
moments.text: The memorial to Joyce Kilmer is an uncut forest, with trees more than 400 years old. In 1934, the New York Bozeman Bulger Post of the Veterans of Foreign Wars asked for a forest memorial to the poet killed in World War I. The Forest Service chose 3,800 acres along Little Santeetlah Creek and dedicated the tract in 1936. A two-mile trail now traces a figure eight through the forest, meeting at a memorial plaque. Among the old-growth hardwoods, the oldest yellow-poplars stand 100 feet tall and measure more than 20 feet around.
moments.notice: Look for the memorial plaque where the two trail loops meet.
